subcohort.notes: Country-level cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) are captured via the 'subgroups' and 'country' fields instead.

control.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.

country.evidence_quote: For Ghana, 44 individuals were included... For Ethiopia 50 individuals... And for Tanzania 68 individuals

days_from_first_collection.notes: Study is cross-sectional for these cohorts; no longitudinal day offsets reported.

age.notes: Reported as mean age per subgroup with SD and range; representative mean values used here. Full SD/range: Ghana_adults SD6.61 range20-45; Ghana_children SD3.67 range0-15; Ethiopia_adults SD6.24 range22-45; Ethiopia_infants SD1.05 range0.167-4.5; Tanzania_adults SD8.88 range18-61; Tanzania_children SD4.74 range0-18.

age_group.notes: Age ranges for 'children'/'infants' subgroups span multiple standard age_group categories (e.g., 0-15 yrs spans Newborn to Adolescent); classification based on mean/majority age is approximate.

ancestry.notes: Only nationality/country of residence given, not formal ancestry categories.

family.evidence_quote: In Ghana 12 extended families from the Asante Akim North district region were sampled
family.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
family.notes: Number of families per country given (Ghana=12, Tanzania=18, Ethiopia=24 mother-infant pairs) but individual family identifiers not provided.

family_role.evidence_quote: This cohort included 24 mothers and their infant(s) for a total of 50 metagenomes.
family_role.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
family_role.notes: Ghana and Tanzania described as 'extended families' without specifying mother/father/child roles for adults vs children.

sex.notes: Sex reported as aggregate population percentages per adult subgroup, not as a single categorical value per individual; not reported for child/infant subgroups.

zigosity.notes: No twin/zygosity information reported in the paper.

age_min.notes: Age ranges reported per country/age-group subgroup; min value extracted from reported range.

age_max.notes: Age ranges reported per country/age-group subgroup; max value extracted from reported range.

age_years.notes: Mean age reported per subgroup with standard deviation; represents study-level average age per subgroup, not per-participant.

antibiotics_current_use.notes: Not reported for the sequenced cohorts.

bmi.notes: BMI mentioned as a factor analyzed in disease association meta-analysis but no values given for the sequenced cohorts; text states 'we considered if the P.copri complex could be associated with other factors such as body mass index (BMI) or age' without reporting values.

dietary_restriction.notes: No specific dietary restriction data reported for participants.

disease.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
disease.notes: Applies to all six subgroups (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania adults/children/infants).

disease_details.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
disease_details.notes: Same as 'disease' field; no more specific disease terms reported for these cohorts.

disease_response_orr.notes: No treatment response data in this study.

feces_phenotype.notes: Stool samples were collected for metagenomic sequencing but no specific fecal clinical phenotype (e.g., consistency score) reported.

fmt_id.notes: No FMT study design in this paper.

fmt_role.notes: No FMT study design in this paper.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Although infants (Ethiopia) and children were sampled, no specific feeding method (breastfeeding/formula) data reported.

obgyn_pregnancy.notes: Not reported, though Ethiopia and Ghana adult subgroups are 100%/52.2% female, pregnancy status not specified.

treatment.notes: No treatment administered to the sequenced non-Westernized cohort participants; treatment context only mentioned for isolate donors (rheumatoid arthritis patients) unrelated to demographic cohorts.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: CRC datasets referenced from other studies but no tumor staging data given in this paper.

biomarker_name.notes: No clinical biomarker panel (e.g., blood biomarkers) reported; paper focuses on genomic/metagenomic analysis of P. copri.

disease_response_os.notes: No survival/disease outcome data reported; this is a microbial genomics study, not a clinical trial.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal/stool samples were collected and analyzed for microbial content but no discrete 'feces phenotype value' metric was reported.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Colorectal cancer (CRC) cohorts were referenced in disease-association analyses but no tumor size measurements were reported in this paper.

value: Study analyzed 6,874 publicly available metagenomes from 36 individual datasets across six continents and 25 countries
Reconstructed 1,023 P. copri genomes (17 isolates, 1,006 MAGs) forming four distinct clades (A, B, C, D)
Non-Westernized cohorts newly sequenced: Ghana (44 individuals), Ethiopia (50 individuals), Tanzania (68 individuals)
Ancient samples analyzed: Iceman (5,300-year-old ice mummy) and three Mexican coprolites (~1,300 BP) from La Cueva de los Muertos Chiquitos
P. copri clade divergence estimated to have begun ~6.5 million years ago, predating human migration out of Africa
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: we performed an analysis of 6,874 publicly available metagenomes from 36 individual datasets (Table S1), representing six continents and 25 different countries.
uncurated_metadata.section: Results — Analysis of >1,000 P. copri Genomes
uncurated_metadata.notes: General study metadata not fitting other schema fields; included for context.

host_species.evidence_quote: Prevotella copri is a frequent inhabitant of the human intestinal microbiome
host_species.notes: Confirmed throughout paper via human stool sample collection, human subjects from Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania, and human archaeological (Iceman, coprolite) samples.

extraction_warnings: This paper reports aggregate cohort-level statistics (means, SDs, percentages) for the newly sequenced Ghana, Ethiopia, and Tanzania cohorts rather than per-subject or per-sample rows; granularity was set to subgroup_level and no sample-level rows were fabricated.
study_name, subject_id, sample_id, and curator were not explicitly reported in the extracted text and are marked not_reported.
The 'control' field value ('Study Control') was inferred with low confidence since these healthy non-Westernized individuals were not part of a formal disease case-control comparison in this study.

The 'sex' field for adult subgroups is reported as population percentages (not a single Female/Male value), which does not map cleanly onto the enum; verbatim percentage text was preserved for downstream harmonization.
age_group assignments for children/infant subgroups are approximate because reported age ranges (e.g., 0-15 yrs, 0-18 yrs) span multiple standard age_group categories.
Numbers reported for Ghana (44 total = 23 adults + 25 children = 48) appear internally inconsistent in the source text; extracted values are verbatim as printed.
PMID was taken from the paper_id input tag rather than being explicitly printed in the extracted paper text.

This paper is primarily a microbial genomics/metagenomics study; most clinical/host-phenotype schema fields (zygosity, BMI, disease response, neonatal, obgyn, HLA, treatment, tumor staging) are not applicable/reported.

Demographic data (age, sex) for the three newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) are reported stratified by country and age-group (adult vs child/infant), justifying subgroup_level granularity.
Disease status 'Healthy' applies uniformly across all six defined subgroups based on the statement 'free of self-reported disease'.
Sex distribution (e.g., 52.2% female for Ghana adults) was reported but sex is not part of the provided schema, so it was not extracted despite being available in the text.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('subgroup_level'); kept batch 0.
Batch 2 subgroups [] differ from batch 0 ['Ghana_adults', 'Ghana_children', 'Ethiopia_adults', 'Ethiopia_infants', 'Tanzania_adults', 'Tanzania_children']; kept batch 0.

This paper is a microbial genomics/metagenomics study (P. copri population genomics), not a clinical trial or biomarker study. Most schema fields (biomarker_name/unit/value, disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, feces_phenotype_value, tumor_size_measurement, tumor_size_residual_measurement) are not applicable/not reported in this context.

Colorectal cancer (CRC), T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, and IBD cohorts were referenced only in the context of P. copri clade prevalence/abundance association analyses (Figure S2), not as primary clinical outcome data for this study.

No sample-level (per-participant) data table was found in the provided text; all reported values are study-level or dataset/cohort-level aggregates (e.g., prevalence percentages by Westernization status).
